title: kpidash service status
description: Payload of kpidash:services:{name}:{host} — latest-value, no TTL, reader-owned staleness via ts, where the window is the CONSUMER'S and is per service rather than a number this schema fixes: kpidash's default is 60 s, and a daily publisher gets its own (`kmon` has had 26 h since kpidash sprint 018, and publishes this key once per nightly). See kpidash's docs/CLIENT-PROTOCOL.md §8a. There is deliberately no cadence field in the payload — the shape has two consumers and adding one was declined (korg:2309). Key is always 4 segments; {host} sentinel `_` means no host. Identity is (name, host); the key is authoritative over any payload echo. Since kdashdata sprint 028 a publisher may lay out a multi-line card with the optional `title`, `lines` and `span`; `text` stays required as the one-line fallback for every reader that does not know them. The border colour is deliberately NOT client-controlled: it stays a function of `state` and freshness on the reader's side, so a dead publisher still goes red whatever it last asked for.

ts.description: Unix seconds (float) of last payload; drives staleness

text.description: Short status text shown on the card

host.description: Echo of the key's host segment, display only

icon.description: Optional icon index (kpidash lv_font_icons_56); absent means no icon

title.description: Card heading. Absent: the key's {name}, as before sprint 028.

lines.description: Body lines, top to bottom. When present and non-empty a reader draws these INSTEAD of `text`; empty or absent, it draws `text`. A reader that finds `lines` malformed drops the whole array and falls back to `text` — a card that vanishes is worse than one that reads plainly.

items.description: A bare string is shorthand for {"t": <string>} with every default. The string keyword here (`pattern`) applies to the shorthand, the object keywords (`required`, `properties`) to the long form — JSON Schema applies each keyword only to the instance type it is about.

t.description: The line. "" is a blank spacer line. No newlines inside.

size.description: Coarse size; absent: M. The reader maps these to fonts it already has.

align.description: Alignment; absent: C, which is how `text` is drawn.

color.description: Text colour, #rrggbb. Absent: the reader's default foreground.

span.description: Card width in card units. Absent: 1.

x-counterexamples.why: the state enum is lower-case and closed; a capitalised twin renders as an unknown state, which is the colour a reader least expects
`text` is required — a service card with a colour and no words is a light nobody can act on
`unhealthy` is the word this contract uses for that; a synonym is a new state the consumer has no ladder for
`lines` holds at most 8; a ninth has nowhere to go on a card, and clipping it silently would hide the line the publisher put last on purpose
`size` is the closed S/M/L set a reader maps to fonts it has; XL names a font no reader promises
`color` is #rrggbb only; a colour name is a vocabulary every reader would have to agree on
a line object must carry `t`; a styled nothing is not a spacer — `""` is
a line is one line; a newline inside it is layout the reader never agreed to, so it is two entries
`span` is 1 or 2 card units; a wider card is a layout the dashboard has no slot for
`text` stays required even with `lines`: it is the fallback for every reader that does not know `lines`, and for one that finds them malformed
